Findings.Comment: The retry guard is inverted relative to the retry policy. `retryable` returns true for transient errors (anything not wrapped in `ErrPermanent`), so `if retryable(lastErr) { return lastErr }` aborts on the first transient failure (e.g. a 503 or connection error) and never retries, while permanent errors (e.g. a 404 or 410 status from `post`) fall through to the loop and are retried up to `maxAttempts` times — exactly backwards from the documented behavior in `Deliver`'s comment and from the pre-change `if !retryable(err) { return err }`. The log line "notification delivery failed, will retry" also now fires for permanent rejections that are then needlessly retried.

Findings.Comment: The two error-wrapping branches are swapped relative to the documented contract. When `Scan` returns no rows (`errors.Is(err, errNoRows)` true), the function returns `err` itself instead of `ErrNoClaim`, so a caller checking `errors.Is(result, ErrNoClaim)` to detect an unclaimed project sees `false` and treats it as a database fault. Conversely, any real database fault (connection loss, timeout) is wrapped with `ErrNoClaim`, so the same caller treats the project as unowned — which on a claim path can let a team claim a project that is in fact already owned. The removed lines had the branches the right way round; the doc comment on `ErrNoClaim` ("what callers match on when a project has no owner yet") states the invariant this diff breaks.

Findings.Comment: This swap inverts the error contract documented just above the function: `ErrNoClaim` is declared as what callers match on when a project has no owner, and the comment promises callers can distinguish "nobody owns it" from a database fault with `errors.Is`. After the change, the `errNoRows` branch wraps the raw driver error (so `errors.Is(err, ErrNoClaim)` is false exactly when there is no claim), while any real database fault is wrapped with `ErrNoClaim` (so `errors.Is(err, ErrNoClaim)` is true exactly when the database is broken). A caller that gates project claiming on `errors.Is(err, store.ErrNoClaim)` will now treat a connection failure as an unowned project and fail to detect genuinely unowned projects. The two branches must wrap the opposite errors from what they do now.
Findings.Headline: Store.Owner inverts ErrNoClaim and the raw driver error

Expected.why: The branches wrap each other's error: errors.Is(err, ErrNoClaim) is now false when the project is genuinely unclaimed and true when the query failed, so a database fault is treated as an unowned project.
